items.stem: An organization wants to reduce the risk that an automated hiring model systematically disadvantages a protected group. Which responsible-AI principle most directly addresses this?

options.text: Fairness, including bias assessment and mitigation
options.rationale: Correct: fairness and bias assessment directly address systematic disadvantage to protected groups.
Inference speed is a performance concern, not a fairness safeguard.
Cost control is unrelated to fairness.
Marketing reach is a business metric, not a responsible-AI principle.

items.explanation: Correct: fairness and bias assessment directly address systematic disadvantage to protected groups.

items.stem: In AI governance, maintaining model documentation such as intended use, data sources and limitations primarily supports which principle?

options.rationale: Correct: documenting intended use, data and limitations supports transparency and accountability.
Documentation is not an energy-efficiency measure.
This is unrelated to governance documentation.

items.explanation: Correct: documenting intended use, data and limitations supports transparency and accountability.

items.stem: Select TWO activities that form part of operating AI governance across the model lifecycle. (Select TWO.)

options.text: Ongoing monitoring of model performance and drift
options.rationale: Correct: monitoring for performance and drift is core to operating governance.

options.text: Maintaining documentation and conducting testing or audits
options.rationale: Correct: documentation and testing/audits operationalize governance.

options.text: Deleting all logs to save space
options.rationale: Destroying logs undermines accountability and governance.
Governance requires meeting, not ignoring, requirements.
Removing oversight is contrary to responsible governance.

items.explanation: Correct: monitoring for performance and drift is core to operating governance.
